summary: Implemented and independently validated a persistent, workspace-scoped MCP registry with allowlisted registration, authenticated lifecycle operations, capability discovery, provenance-labelled tools, revocation, append-only audit events, and exact read-tool exposure to the OpenAI Agents runtime. The live Docker MCP Gateway and GitHub Official MCP server were exercised without exposing credentials.

files.purpose: Strict lifecycle, registry, tool-risk and provenance contracts
Bounded streamable-HTTP handshake and sanitized capability discovery
Workspace registry, allowlist, lifecycle, revocation and fail-closed runtime materialization
Public sanitized registry reads and administrator-authenticated mutations
Connect only enabled registry servers and expose exact persisted read tools
Runtime D1 schema, indexes and append-only lifecycle triggers
Durable Drizzle schema for MCP registry and events
Fresh-install MCP schema, indexes and append-only triggers
Authenticated internal gateway endpoint, explicit host/port and runtime-only secret file
Protocol, URL policy, provenance and sanitized failure tests
Allowlist, admin gate, durable lifecycle, revocation and read-only runtime tests

scopeExpansion.reason: The roadmap requires a persistent registry. The site uses D1, so the runtime CREATE TABLE path alone was insufficient for fresh installs and releases; a generated, inspected migration is required.

securityEvidence: Registration options exposed only id, label and transport; no URL or secret reference was returned.
Connected registry response contained no bearer header, authorization value, secret reference, personal-access-token name or internal gateway URL.
A tool is read-only only when the MCP server provides readOnlyHint=true and does not mark it destructive; unknown or deceptively named unannotated tools default to external/approval-required.
Recursive metadata sanitization removes the configured credential and generic credential patterns from capabilities, descriptions and input schemas before persistence or API output.
Only 26 explicitly annotated read tools are eligible for agent runtime exposure; 18 side-effect tools remain approval-labelled and fail closed until P3-T2 adds invocation-time policy enforcement.
Revocation disabled the server immediately and required explicit re-registration before another connect.
knownLimits: Per-workspace and per-agent policy plus invocation-time revocation enforcement belongs to P3-T2; all side-effect tools remain unavailable meanwhile.
The Docker MCP Gateway image remains a floating latest tag until P6-T1 pins and scans production images.
Lifecycle mutation authentication is a server-side administrator token until the operator identity work is completed.
